subject: MAP: unit economics assumptions & evaluation plan for Acme Cloud
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Michael Tran <michael.tran@acmecloud.com>, Priya Desai <priya.desai@acmecloud.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 22 Apr 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: MAP draft + unit-econ workbook (first pass)

Michael / Priya — attaching the first-pass MAP and a lightweight unit-econ workbook for your evaluation team. Key asks below so we can lock the evaluation plan and close timeline: 

1) Confirm token assumptions: what does a "session" look like for you? (avg user prompt tokens, avg assistant response tokens, and expected calls per session)
2) Confirm cache/reuse behavior: do you expect high prefix reuse across calls (chat-style context reuse) or mostly unique prompts?
3) Ops SLOs that will drive batching & latency tradeoffs (p95 latency target, allowed batching window)

Baseline numbers in the workbook are conservative but we want your input so the MAP includes realistic unit-econ breakpoints (tokens/$ at 20/50/80% cache hit).

Proposed timeline (we can move if needed):
- 4/25: Redwood sends tuned token model + eval plan (we'll seed with 1k prompts)
- 5/6: Acme completes internal eval and provides feedback + quality metrics
- 5/13: Procurement & security checklist review starts
- 5/20: Target signed PO / reserved capacity commitment
- 6/01: Production traffic ramp begins

Attachment: acme_map_v1.xlsx (MAP + task owner list) and token_econ_model_v2.csv (simple per-scenario calc)

Thanks — happy to jump on a short call if you want to walk through the workbook.

Jonas Weber
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: MAP draft + unit-econ workbook (first pass)

Thanks Jonas — quick clarifying questions from our side before we run the eval: 

- What token counts are you using in the workbook per transaction (input vs output)? Can you provide a few realistic examples (search query -> assistant reply; customer-support chat -> agent reply)?
- For caching: are you modeling prefix/KV cache (i.e., repeated context) or response-level caching? What TTL and hit-rate buckets did you test?
- Batching: what batching window and expected average batch size did you assume for latency-sensitive routes? Our SRE will want to know how much headroom we need for spikes — can Redwood support bursts to ~200 RPS for the first 10 minutes of a promo?

We can run a small pilot if we get the assumptions. Also cc'd Priya so procurement knows the timeline.

Michael
Director of Platform Engineering
Acme Cloud
[michael.tran@acmecloud.com]

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: Michael Tran <michael.tran@acmecloud.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 24 Apr 2026 15:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP draft + unit-econ workbook (technical assumptions)

Michael — quick technical breakdown from the infra side (will add a sanitized tab to the workbook):

Assumptions used in token_econ_model_v2.csv (baseline scenario):
- Avg prompt size (user + system + context prefixes): 220 tokens
- Avg model response: 480 tokens
- Total tokens per transaction (round-trip): ~700 tokens

Caching model: 
- Prefix / KV cache hit-rate buckets modeled: 0% / 25% / 50% / 75%
- Effective token reduction on a prefix hit: 40% of generation tokens saved (we avoid re-generating repeated context and only generate the new suffix)
- TTL guidance: short-lived session cache (60s) for conversational flows, longer for templated prompts (1h)

Batching & latency: 
- Batching window assumed for cost model: 50ms (default for low-latency routes); avg batch size ~3 at our typical production QPS pattern -> ~2.3x GPU throughput improvement vs single-request dispatch
- For high-latency-tolerant background jobs we model a 200ms window -> avg batch size ~8 -> ~5x throughput improvement

Cost numbers (compute cost to Redwood, not list price):
- Baseline compute: $0.25 per 1M tokens (no batching / no cache) -> tokens per $ = 4,000,000
- With 2.3x batching improvement and 25% cache hit: effective compute cost ~ $0.10 per 1M tokens -> tokens per $ = 10,000,000 (illustrative)
- We included a sensitivity tab that shows tokens/$ across cache hit 0-75% and batch sizes 1-8.

Burst capacity: our hosted tier supports short bursts; we recommend a warm reserve for guaranteed 200 RPS spikes during promos. We can size a small dedicated pool (or reserved burst) as part of the MAP — I put a placeholder in the workbook.

I've attached a sanitized summary and will add a short notes tab to the MAP. Let me know if you want these numbers adjusted to match your observed prompt histograms.

--
Priyom Das
Solutions Engineer, Inference Ops
Redwood Inference
[attachment: token_econ_model_v2.csv (CSV)]

Michael — thanks for the rapid feedback. I've updated the MAP (attached) with Priyom's technical assumptions and two alternative cost scenarios (conservative / optimistic). Short summary and next actions below: 

Summary: 
- Baseline round-trip token assumption used for evaluation: 700 tokens/tx (220 input / 480 output)
- We will test cache hit buckets 0/25/50/75% during the seeded eval; please flag which bucket you expect to be closest to reality.
- Latency route: we will run the seed eval with a 50ms batching window and capture p50/p95/p99.
- Procurement: Monica will drop SOC2 and pricing terms into the HubSpot deal this week.

Action items (owners / due dates):
- Acme: provide a 1k prompt sample and an expected promo spike profile — due 2026-05-02 (Michael / Priya)
- Redwood (Priyom): run seed eval and return token-level logs + quality metrics — due 2026-04-25 (moved to 4/25 earlier; completed)
- Redwood (Jonas): update MAP with procurement checklist + PO template — due 2026-05-06
- Both: schedule a 30m sync to review results week of 5/11

Attachment: acme_map_v1.xlsx (updated), token_econ_model_v2.csv (sensitivity tab added)

If that all looks good I'll mark the MAP as "active" in HubSpot and we can start the seeded run.

Jonas Weber
